summary: Whether comparisons keep their source form (V <= c) or the analysis-canonical rewrite (V < c+1).
use_when: Flip to canonical only to reproduce upstream Ghidra output; original (default) is more faithful to source.
symptoms: comparison constant off by one versus upstream ghidra (x <= 9 vs x < 10)
need the analysis-canonical compare form to diff against upstream ghidra output

summary: Whether a passively-active second return register may be joined into a wide return (pair) or dropped (single).
use_when: Set single PER FUNCTION when a void/single-register function shows a spurious CONCAT44 return (e.g. SPARC); DESTRUCTIVE as a global default (truncates real multi-register returns).
symptoms: spurious CONCAT44 return value in a void or single-register function
two return registers joined into one double-width return (e.g. sparc o0/o1)
return type twice the natural width built from a register concat

summary: Decompile a whole binary callees-first and state each function's RECOVERED parameter types where its callers read declared ones from, so what one function learned about its own parameters reaches every call to it. `TypeOpCall::getInputLocal` (typeop.cc:689) already types a call argument from the callee's parameter -- but only from a DECLARED prototype, and the only writers of that slot are facts from outside the decompile: a libc/`libctypes` table entry, a DWARF or demangled signature, `--assert prototype`, `parse line extern`. Nothing states what a RECOVERY found, so an internal callee tells its callers nothing and each caller types the call from its own local evidence alone. coreutils fmt -O2 shows the cost: `sub_3700` recovers as `unsigned long sub_3700(FILE *a0, unsigned long a1)` and its caller still renders `sub_3700(stdin,v7)` with `char *v7` typed from nothing. With the option on, `kuna decompile-all` orders the run by the call graph `kuna xrefs` already publishes (`kuna_analysis::listing::xrefs`, the same edges `--reachable-from` walks), decompiles each callee before its callers over Tarjan's SCCs of those edges, and records the parameter types the callee recovered against the storage it recovered them in. Inside a recursive component (a function that calls itself, or a cycle of functions calling each other) `callees first` has no meaning: `cycles` (the default) still lets every member state its types, decompiling a larger component's members once each in a depth-first order over the component's own calls that starts from the members something outside it calls, so each member reads the partners it reaches and the component's callers read every member; `types` states nothing for a member of a recursive component, which stops the chain at the first recursion (every coreutils caller that passes a file name to gnulib's self-recursive `quotearg_buffer_restyled` kept it an integer). At each later call site, argument `i` takes the callee's recovered type for parameter `i` when the two agree about the storage -- position and storage both, so the two recoveries are talking about the same argument. Results are buffered and emitted in address order, so only the decompile ORDER changes and the output stays byte-stable. A function never reads its own statement, and before `structsynth`'s convergence sweep decompiles anything again it forgets every stated list that names a superseded structure (a redone callee states again before its redone callers), so a redone recursive function never takes the structure the redo exists to replace from its own first answer or a cycle partner's. `types` and `cycles` state ONLY parameter types: nothing is locked, so `ActionFuncLink` runs the caller's own argument recovery at every call exactly as it does with the option off and no call gains an argument; the one argument a call can lose is the trailing clobbered one `argclobber` drops on the evidence of a stated list, under `cycles` at a recursive callee too. The recovered type arrives as one more vote in `Varnode::getLocalType`'s `type_order` fold; it is never the type a cast is measured against, so where it loses the argument renders as it does off, and it is refused outright where the caller holds evidence the fold cannot weigh: the argument is the address of a frame object, the value (its COPY/CAST/MULTIEQUAL/INDIRECT family) is declared, global, a frame address, frame memory, an element of a stack struct, array or indexed frame region, or loaded through itself (`p = *p`), the vote is deeper than the inferred pointer cap, a pointer vote lands on a constant inside a function's code (a Thumb address would render as `&sub_8130[1]`, a subscript of a function), another call reads or writes the same value as a different kind (pointer, integer, float), float-ness disagrees with the value or its register, or what the caller loads and stores through a pointer disagrees with a float, composite or non-character primitive pointee (an access or address outside the object, an access across or inside its members, a step of other than one element, integer bits moved through a float member, or a constant stored wider than a non-character primitive pointee, which `SplitDatatype` would print as one store per element; a caller with too many derived addresses to check is refused as well). The callee's recovered return type is not stated: a call's result has no competing evidence, so a wrong one spreads into the caller. `lock` instead parks the recovered prototype in the symbol table, where `ActionDefaultParams` reads a declared one from, which does decide the call's arity: the parked list is a FLOOR rather than a ceiling (the first slot past the recovered parameters starts a variable tail, so `func_link_input` keeps active-input recovery on and a caller that passes more still recovers the rest), and four further rules read the callee's own machine code through the entry-liveness walk `calleedeadarg` owns -- a trailing parameter the body never reads is trimmed rather than stated, a callee that provably READS the register its next argument would arrive in has under-recovered and is declined, a recovered list that saturates the convention's argument registers is declined (the shape a variadic register-save prologue leaves: exactly six parameters on SysV, exactly four on AAPCS), and a list the model would not place in the storage it was recovered in is declined outright. Every mode declines when the function's decompile errored, when it says nothing, when model selection did not settle, when a parameter is a hidden return pointer, and -- always -- when a prototype is already DECLARED for that entry; `types` and `lock` also decline for a function in a recursive component, so an operator's `--assert prototype`, a libc signature, DWARF or a demangled name outranks anything recovery found. The statement is a caller-side fact only: the locked-input branch of `ActionPrototypeTypes` is stubbed, and the callee has already been decompiled when its types are stated.
use_when: On by default (`cycles`) on a whole-binary `kuna decompile-all`; a whole-binary surface otherwise, except that a single-function `kuna decompile` on a compiler spec with preferred register splits bootstraps the recovered parameter types of the direct callees whose own call sites pass a preferred-split register in an active input trial (at most 32, no recursion, isolated from the caller's own drive state, types only). The same drive also states, before its own pipeline runs, the recovered prototype of each callee the function tail-calls (at most 4, each of at most 512 instructions), so a thunk `xor esi,esi; jmp target` prints `return target(a0,NULL)` and a forwarder passes through the arguments its callee reads, as the whole-binary run prints them; a narrowed `decompile-all` (`--addr`, `--functions`, `--limit`, a triage filter) and `kuna decompile --json` state the same tail callees for each function they select, where a selected forwarder otherwise printed `target(); // tail-call` with the arguments it forwards dropped. That bootstrap is what lets a split-register argument take the callee's type; a value merely loaded from a `q` register but passed only through integer registers selects nothing, and it never states arity; batch/--jobs/decompile-project keep the schedules below. A run narrowed by `--functions`, `--addr` or a triage filter, selecting one function, or on a `--raw-image` (which has no call graph), decompiles in address order and builds no call graph unless the option is named, which orders the selection and notes on stderr that a callee outside it states nothing. `decompile-project` and `decompile-graph` have their own schedules and are not callee-first either; both warn on stderr when the option is asked for explicitly. `types` is the same statement without recursive components: set it if a caller's argument takes a type from a recursive callee whose own recovery is wrong about it (a member of a cycle is decompiled before the partners that call back into it, so what it states was recovered without their statements; over the 444-slice campaign corpus `cycles` moves 46 functions onto a perfect type_match and none off, 162 up and 1 down, and renders the same call arguments at every site of 15 binaries). Leave it on when a type the caller clearly knows -- a `FILE *` from `fopen`, a `char *` from `getenv` -- stops at a call and the callee's parameter stays `long`, or when the same internal callee's parameters are typed at one site and not at another. `types` and `cycles` lock no call spec, so no call gains an argument, and a vote is refused where the caller's own evidence contradicts it; the one argument a call can lose is the trailing clobbered one `argclobber` (on by default) drops where the callee's stated list and body both say the register is free, which under `cycles` includes a recursive callee (`rtarget(a0,5)` where `types` and `off` render `rtarget(a0,5,v3)`). It does change spellings, so read a changed function rather than assume it is cosmetic: a vote that wins adds a cast at the argument it types (`caller((unsigned char *)0x402000,3)`), a character pointee guessed for a pointer can split one wide constant store through it into character stores of the same bytes (`*(unsigned long *)(a0 + 0xa0) = 0` becomes eight `'\0'` stores -- the same memory contents, a different access width, which matters on memory-mapped I/O; text prints as `builtin_strncpy`, and a pointee of any other primitive type narrower than a constant stored through the pointer is refused, a buffer filled a word at a time included) or widen a narrow load into a truncation of the wider element (`*(short *)(a0 + 0xc)` becomes `(short)a0[3]` -- the same value, read at a different width), and an unsigned vote can make a caller's parameter unsigned, with casts keeping its signed uses (`(int)a0 >> 2`). A float vote is stricter than the others: it is refused unless every other use of the value is a float or a copy of its bits, so a word the caller also adds, compares, truncates, takes bytes out of or stores, or returns or passes on outside a float register, stays an integer -- where a float travels in a general register (MIPS o32, ARM softfp) a float vote there printed `(short)((unsigned int)v1 >> 0x10)` and `a2[1] = (int)v1`, value conversions of the bits. A pointer vote is held to the same standard one level down: where the caller's own loads and stores through the pointer disagree with the pointee -- an access or address outside it, an access across or inside its members, a step of other than one element, or integer bits moved through a float member -- the vote is refused, so `*a0 = (double)(a1 + 1)` never prints for a union a callee sums as doubles. Measured over 60 stripped binaries (32,406 functions: x86-64 userland, ARM Cortex-M firmware and two PE files) against main with structsynth on: the same call arguments in both arms (every one of more than 258,000), zero functions gaining a parameter of their own, no stack object split, no stack local read without a write, and no new array subscript of a structure or piece assignment; over the 444-slice campaign corpus more than 110 functions reach a perfect type_match and none leave it. Flip to `off` if a caller's parameter or local takes a type from a callee whose own recovery is wrong about it and nothing at the call site contradicts it -- the vote only loses to contrary evidence, not to a better guess. `lock` is the opt-in arity claim: it also states how many parameters the callee has, which collapses a caller that over-recovered (`ext2fs_mmp_start` renders 3 arguments and takes 1) and gains 818 call arguments at 418 sites over the x86-64 half of a 22-binary corpus -- but it FABRICATES parameters where the callee's own recovery over-counted, 155 of 7,553 x86-64 functions and 630 of 6,589 ARM Cortex-M ones gaining an argument row nothing sets, which `type_match` cannot see at all because a decompiled variable with no ground-truth counterpart is never a false positive. Use `lock` on a program where you have checked that, not as a default, and prefer `argclobber` where the complaint is a trailing register argument a previous call left behind -- `argclobber` declines a locked-and-variadic call spec, so `lock` disables it at every stated site, while `types` and `cycles` compose with it (under `cycles` a recursive callee's stated list is evidence for `argclobber` too, and its callee-body walk proves nothing about a register handed on into a cycle). Mutually exclusive with `--jobs N` when asked for explicitly (each worker process loads the binary into its own `Architecture`, so a stated type cannot cross a chunk boundary), exactly like `--assert`; a `--jobs` run under the default states nothing and says so on stderr, and `--option protoorder off` makes it byte-identical to the serial run. Set `KUNA_PROTOORDER_TRACE=1` to have each statement and each decline printed with its reason on stderr.
inspiration: angr's callee-first pipeline: `Clinic` propagates a recovered `SimTypeFunction` back onto the callee's `Function.prototype` and later callers read it (`analyses/decompiler/clinic.py`), which is why angr commits 43.4% of its arguments to a pointer type on coreutils fmt where kuna commits 30.6%. Ghidra reaches the same place with its decompiler-parameter-ID analyzer, which commits recovered prototypes to the program database before the functions that call them are decompiled.
symptoms: a FILE * or char * the caller holds becomes long at the callee's parameter
a function that only hands a string on to a recursive function (quotearg_buffer_restyled, a tree walk, a pair of functions calling each other) keeps an integer parameter
an argument is typed at one call site of a callee and not at another
decompiling one function alone gives it a prototype the whole-binary output does not use at its call sites
the same sub_ address is called with one argument at one site and three at another in the same function

summary: Keep the gotos into a shared RETURN block when splitting it would clone more than <n> ops (default 1,048,576). ActionReturnSplit gives every goto into a RETURN block its own copy of the whole block, every op once per split edge. A bare epilogue is a few ops, but a RETURN block also carries one `glob = glob` guard COPY per global the function reads (Heritage::guardReturns), so a huge function that reads thousands of globals and reaches one return from hundreds of gotos clones millions of ops, which every later pass and the variable merge then walk: serde-hkx's 194 KB deserializer has two return blocks of 4,524 ops reached by 674 and 658 gotos, 6.0 million cloned ops (8.75 million ops in the function right after the split, 7.19 million of them guard COPYs). The cost is the block's op count times its split edges; a block under the limit splits exactly as upstream, so the C changes only in a function that would have cloned more, where those paths print `goto` to the shared return instead of their own `return`. `off` restores the unlimited split.
use_when: On by default at 1048576. Lower it to keep a large function's return gotos when splitting them costs memory, or set it off to always give every goto its own return, as upstream does.
inspiration: GH-1034 serde-hkx 0.7.3's hkxc.exe at 0x1406198f0: splitting two shared return blocks of 4,524 ops reached by 674 and 658 gotos cloned 6.0 million ops, and the function passed 15 GB.
symptoms: a huge function exhausts memory right after its return blocks are split
millions of COPY ops of a global into itself fill a large function's IR
a function with hundreds of gotos to one return and thousands of globals takes gigabytes to decompile

summary: Apply the DEMANGLED C++ signature - the class type for `this` plus the declared parameter types - to every function whose mangled symbol survives, which on a STRIPPED C++ shared library is the whole exported API in .dynsym and the only signature source left. Parses the full c++filt-style form (the same string the Ghidra GNU demangler parses), maps a class-shaped parameter to a named opaque structure reachable only as a pointee, refuses any by-value aggregate or overloaded operator, and parks the prototype by entry ADDRESS. The return type is deliberately NOT applied: Itanium encodes one only for a template function, so the function keeps whatever kuna's own recovery finds. Three-valued because Itanium mangling cannot tell a static member function from a non-static one and adding a `this` that is not there shifts every following parameter: `proven` applies only the shapes the mangling entails (constructors, destructors, cv-/ref-qualified members, unqualified globals, explicit MSVC access/static/convention), `inferred` also decides the ambiguous nested names from class evidence mined out of the binary's own symbols.
use_when: proven (default) is precision 1.0000 / recall 0.7093 on google/leveldb: `void leveldb::Cache::~Cache(Cache *this)` instead of `void leveldb::Cache::~Cache(unsigned long a0)`. Raise to inferred for precision 0.9278 / recall 0.9978 - it additionally recovers plain (non-const, non-ctor) member functions like `leveldb::TableBuilder::WriteBlock(TableBuilder *this,BlockBuilder *a1,BlockHandle *a2)` and namespaced free functions like `leveldb::NewMemEnv(Env *a0)`, at the cost of a spurious `this` on a static member. Flip off to restore name-only demangling.
symptoms: c++ member functions on a stripped binary decompile with a0/a1 parameters
this renders as int8 * or unsigned long instead of the class type
a mangled symbol names the function but not its parameter types
no signature recovery on a stripped c++ shared library

summary: On an arm64e Mach-O, select the Apple-Silicon pointer-authentication SLEIGH spec. A Mach-O whose header reports cpusubtype CPU_SUBTYPE_ARM64E loads with the AARCH64:LE:64:AppleSilicon language (the vendored Apple-Silicon v8.5-A spec, which models the pointer-auth/AMX extensions) instead of the generic AARCH64:LE:64:v8A. Pointer authentication does NOT change import naming or symbols (the __stubs indirect-symbol walk is unaffected) — only the spec selection differs (design 3.7). Spec selection is a LOAD-time decision (language_id_for), which runs before any console `option` command, so the live gate is the KUNA_MACHO_ARM64E env var: the kuna CLI exports it for `--option macho-arm64e off`, the console `option` arm sets it for a later `load file` in the same process, and this option name also records the requested state on the Architecture for catalog consistency. A non-arm64e Mach-O, a non-Mach-O target, and every ELF/PE/COFF path are byte-identical, so all parity gates are structurally untouched.
use_when: On by default: an arm64e (Apple-Silicon, pointer-auth) Mach-O decompiles under the AppleSilicon spec that models its extensions. Inert on every non-Mach-O image and on a Mach-O whose cpusubtype is not arm64e. Flip off to load an arm64e image with the generic v8A spec, exactly as any arm64.
inspiration: Ghidra MachoLoader arm64e cpusubtype -> AARCH64:LE:64:AppleSilicon language mapping
symptoms: arm64e mach-o decoded with the generic v8A spec so pointer-auth ops are unmodeled
pac instructions in an apple-silicon binary not modeled by the loaded spec
